China's CXMT Prepares Equipment Investment for New Shanghai Fab… Closing In Fast on Korea

ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's largest DRAM maker, has begun preparing for aggressive capital investment. The company recently started equipment bidding with suppliers for a new fab, while also firming up plans for additional fab expansions. If the investment proceeds without disruption, CXMT is expected to rapidly narrow the production capacity gap with major Korean players such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

According to industry sources on the 11th, CXMT recently launched the equipment bidding process with suppliers for the construction of its new fab in Shanghai.

CXMT currently mass produces DRAM at two fabs in Hefei and one fab in Beijing. Its production capacity is estimated to be in the mid 200,000 wafers per month range at present, and is projected to exceed 300,000 wafers per month by the end of the year.

Plans for additional fab expansions are also taking shape. According to discussions with suppliers and others, CXMT plans to open a new fab in Shanghai in the fourth quarter of this year.

Equipment bidding for that fab has also recently begun. One semiconductor equipment industry source said, "CXMT plans to expand the new Shanghai fab in two phases. Considering the scale of the recent equipment bidding, this fab alone is expected to secure production capacity well above 100,000 wafers per month."

CXMT will then open a new Hefei fab in the first half of next year, followed by a new Beijing fab as early as the second half of next year. It is also targeting the opening of another fab in the Hefei area in the first half of the year after next.

Another equipment industry source explained, "CXMT has recently set the timelines for building multiple fabs in China and is sharing the details. With massive subsidies from the local government and surging memory demand, its determination to expand is strong."

If all of the investment plans are executed, CXMT could steadily add at least 70,000 to 80,000 wafers per month of new production capacity every year from this year through 2028. Some observers project that its production capacity will expand to more than 600,000 wafers per month over the long term.

This is on par with the current production capacity of the leading DRAM makers. Total DRAM production capacity at Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK hynix is estimated at about 700,000 and 600,000 wafers per month, respectively.

However, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have also been accelerating the expansion of their memory chip plants recently. Samsung Electronics has been building a DRAM production line within its Pyeongtaek Campus 4 (P4), and began cleanroom construction for its next generation production base, P5, in the second half of this year.

SK hynix began early operation of M15X in the first quarter of this year and continues to invest to expand its production capacity. It also started placing equipment orders in the third quarter of this year for Y1, its large scale semiconductor cluster in Yongin.

Taiwan's Shin Zu Shing supplies only "golden samples" of foldable iPhone hinges to Apple as production remains unstable

Production of the hinge for the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable phone unveiled on September 9 (local time), was found on September 10 to remain unstable. The hinge was also the component with the greatest impact on delays to the iPhone Duo production schedule.

The original first vendor for the iPhone Duo hinge was Amphenol of the United States, but Shin Zu Shing, which had been the second vendor, is now producing the hinge as the first vendor. This is because Amphenol's production yield fell far short of expectations.

Industry source A said, "Shin Zu Shing's hinge production yield is still low, and at present only 'golden samples' are being selected and sent to Foxconn." This means that among the hinges Shin Zu Shing makes, only those that meet Apple's standards are being picked out one by one and delivered. Another source, B, said, "Some components are experiencing production disruptions, but the Shin Zu Shing hinge is particularly unstable."

Apple designated multiple vendors for most of the remaining components, excluding items such as the organic light emitting diode (OLED) panel made by Samsung Display. Among iPhone Duo components, the hinge is reportedly the only one for which the first vendor is currently experiencing production disruptions.

Apple applied a "3D printed" hinge module to the iPhone Duo. A hinge module is generally made by combining multiple constituent parts, including gears, shafts, and mechanisms for free stop functionality. A 3D printed hinge module can improve the precision of these constituent parts.

When Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo on September 9, it stated that the hinge contains more than 100 constituent parts. Industry source C said, "Making a foldable phone thinner increases the number of hinge parts," adding, "The hinges in thin foldable phones released by Chinese smartphone makers had 120 to 130 parts." He said, "However, the count differs depending on whether hinge parts are limited to those directly tied to the drive mechanism or whether peripheral parts such as bolts and nuts are included," and added, "We will only know precisely after tearing down the iPhone Duo once it launches."

The change of first vendor is also presumed to be a factor behind Apple's difficulties with hinge production. Typically, the first vendor develops the component together with the set maker and finalizes the specifications. The second vendor is at a disadvantage because it must make the component to specifications that the first vendor has already finalized with the set maker. In effect, Shin Zu Shing is producing hinges to specifications that Amphenol previously finalized with Apple.

Supply of the backplate, another key iPhone Duo component, is also tight. The backplate is the part that supports the foldable panel when it is folded or unfolded. Fine holes are formed in the folding region to secure flexibility and durability. The second vendor for the backplate, China's Lingyi iTech, is reportedly struggling with mass production.

Although production of some iPhone Duo components is still not running smoothly, Apple has reportedly provided suppliers with a component production forecast sufficient to build around 5 million to 6 million finished iPhone Duo units by the end of this year. The number of components exceeds the number of finished units because Apple accounts for yield during final assembly as well as replacement demand from damage after the product is sold.

Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo on September 9, but preorders begin a month later on October 16. The launch date is October 23.

iPhone Duo pricing by storage capacity is $1,999 for 256GB (approximately 2.68 million won at current exchange rates), $2,199 for 512GB (approximately 2.95 million won), $2,599 for 1TB (approximately 3.49 million won), and $3,199 for 2TB (approximately 4.29 million won). Korean launch prices are 3.29 million won for 256GB, 3.59 million won for 512GB, 4.19 million won for 1TB, and 5.09 million won for 2TB.

To share the insights I took away:

1. Even if you secure additional GPUs or memory, total system output cannot increase if other segments such as substrates, MLCCs, and wafer testing are in short supply. In other words, in the semiconductor industry, total shipments are determined by the single most constrained component or process.

2. Substrate, power and analog semiconductor, foundry, and memory suppliers have historically been conservative and have not made new greenfield investments until they were confident in long term customer demand. In response, Broadcom, Nvidia, and others signed sufficiently long LTAs with their supply chains and gave them visibility, and that point in time was precisely late 2025 to early 2026. Working backward from there to when a new production fab comes online, meaningful new capacity ramp and production will begin in 2028, not 2027. That means next year, 2027, could be the most supply constrained year in history.

3. In 2028, supply will still be short and the shortage will not be fully resolved, but it will be the year when the largest amount of new production capacity in the history of the semiconductor industry comes online at once. This is an opportunity for additional revenue.

4. The current supply constraint is a safety net that delays overinvestment. In past capital intensive infrastructure booms such as railroads, canals, 3G, and mobile phones, people always overbuilt. But the difference between past cycles and this AI infrastructure cycle is that even with demand in place, production facilities and data centers cannot be built as quickly as desired. So the current supply constraint can paradoxically be seen as playing a positive role in the sense that it limits excessive investment. The explanation is that by the time the supply chain catches up (2028), demand and industry conditions may have normalized to some degree as well. In enterprise AI too, high token costs and limited access to compute are slowing the pace of deployment, and if costs were much lower, companies would have moved more experiments into production environments faster.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics and LG Innotek push to commercialize substrates for Intel's 'EMIB-T', challenging Japan's Ibiden

Samsung Electro-Mechanics and LG Innotek are pursuing the supply of high value added semiconductor substrates for Intel's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB). EMIB is an advanced packaging technology whose demand has recently been growing in the high performance artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor market. Japan's Ibiden is the leading company in this field.

According to industry sources on the 9th, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and LG Innotek are developing and testing products with the goal of entering the package substrate supply chain for Intel's EMIB-T.

Intel's EMIB-T gains traction in the AI chip market, drawing interest from Samsung Electro-Mechanics and LG Innotek

EMIB is an advanced packaging method that has recently been drawing attention in the AI semiconductor industry. Currently, the industry inserts a thin layer called a silicon interposer to connect high bandwidth memory (HBM) and system semiconductors into a single package. Using an interposer allows the circuits of each chip to be connected more densely. This is commonly referred to as '2.5D packaging'.

EMIB connects chips to one another using small silicon bridges instead of an interposer. It is a technology that places silicon bridges only where they are needed. It is more cost efficient than an interposer. Another advantage is that chips can be placed with more flexibility.

Because Intel had previously used EMIB only for manufacturing its own chips, market demand was limited. However, with Intel recently developing an improved version called 'EMIB-T', external sales are now expanding in earnest. Google will also apply EMIB-T for the first time in its next generation AI accelerator (TPU), scheduled for release in the second half of next year.

EMIB-T is a technology that inserts through-silicon vias (TSVs), which serve as power delivery pathways, into the silicon bridge. By shortening the power delivery path between the substrate and the chip through TSVs, it improves power efficiency and signal integrity.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics and LG Innotek have also taken note of the growth of EMIB-T and are attempting to enter the supply chain for its dedicated package substrates. The product embeds a silicon bridge into a flip chip ball grid array (FC-BGA), the existing package substrate for high performance semiconductors, making it technically demanding.

In the case of Samsung Electro-Mechanics, the company is developing the substrate under the concept of a 2.1D package substrate. A person familiar with the matter said, "Samsung Electro-Mechanics has been developing substrate samples for EMIB for several years, and following the recent trend toward EMIB-T commercialization, it is actively pushing to enter the supply chain."

LG Innotek recently sent package substrates for EMIB-T to SK hynix, which is conducting sample tests. LG Innotek and SK hynix are reportedly mounting HBM on the substrate and evaluating the product's characteristics.

Challenging FC-BGA leader Ibiden of Japan, but large scale investment is a burden

Entering the package substrate supply chain for Intel's EMIB-T is one of the key tasks for Samsung Electro-Mechanics and LG Innotek in expanding their high value added FC-BGA businesses, which is their goal.

Currently, package substrates for EMIB-T are supplied by four companies: Ibiden and Shinko Electric of Japan, Unimicron of Taiwan, and AT&S of Austria.

Ibiden is the number one company in the FC-BGA industry. It has built a solid cooperative relationship with Intel. In the first half of this year, it decided to begin construction of a mass production line dedicated to substrates for Intel's EMIB-T, utilizing an existing idle fab. The investment is approximately 2 trillion won. It is reported to have received advance payments from Big Tech companies including Google, Amazon, and Intel.

As latecomers to the relevant supply chain, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and LG Innotek are expected to have to overcome technological and market challenges in order to commercialize substrates for EMIB-T.

An industry official in the substrate sector explained, "Ibiden, Unimicron, and others have built stable technological capabilities and production capacity by mass producing substrates for Intel's EMIB for seven to eight years," adding, "It is true that business opportunities are expanding with EMIB-T, but domestic companies face the risk of having to make large scale investments first."

SK hynix: "Foundry processes could be used for 3D DRAM"

SK hynix said on the 9th that it could use foundry processes in developing 3D DRAM, a next generation memory chip.

At the 2026 SK hynix Future Forum held the previous day at the SUPEX Center on the Icheon campus, SK hynix vice presidents Kim Kyunghoon and Son Hoyoung presented the use of logic foundry processes for DRAM peripheral circuits, maximizing data bus bandwidth, and ultra short distance transmission as the key technology directions for 3D DRAM.

3D DRAM is a next generation DRAM that increases density by stacking memory cells vertically instead of laying them out on a single plane (2D).

Kim and Son explained that realizing this technology requires solving not only design and heat issues but also packaging challenges such as fine interconnects, bonding, and process integration. They also expected that as the boundaries between front end and back end (packaging) processes, and between foundry and memory technologies, draw closer together, joint optimization that goes beyond existing domains will become important.

"3D technology is changing even the technical boundary between the fab and packaging," Son said. "Along with innovation in advanced packaging technology, it is important to build optimization that crosses existing domains and new systems of collaboration."

Shin Changhwan, a professor at Korea University who spoke on the same topic, said, "3D DRAM goes beyond simply stacking chips vertically. It is a technology that breaks down the boundary between memory and logic. With device scaling approaching its limits and the time and power consumed by moving data between the system and memory increasing, the shift to 3D technology is inevitable." He proposed a 3D integrated design framework that links four areas, materials, devices, packaging, and architecture, through artificial intelligence (AI).

In his opening remarks, SK hynix CEO Kwak Nohjung said, "If the memory market of the past was a straight road where the competition was about who could run faster, today it is like driving on a winding road that changes moment to moment. What matters is not only internal capability but also the speed at which we read the pace and direction of change in the external environment and adapt flexibly."

现在的美国经济非常容易被静态数据误导：企业利润率处于二战后最高区间，AI capex 仍在加速，headline 就业依然是正增长。很多人看到这些数据，会得出美国经济依然很强的结论。

但宏观不是一张静态截图，而是一套由收入、消费、利润、投资、就业和信用相互反馈的周期。

利润率越高，不代表未来越安全。恰恰相反，它说明企业定价权已经释放得非常充分，劳动力与其他成本被压制到了极限，消费者承担了利润扩张的大部分代价。利润率继续上升的空间正在缩小，向均值回归的空间却越来越大。

真正需要问的从来不是“今天的利润率有多高”，而是它什么时候见顶，以及什么变量会迫使它掉头。

这个拐点已经开始具备条件。中低收入消费、小商户交易量和 premium discretionary 已经出现 recession-like contraction，个人储蓄率只剩 3%。8 月新增就业看似不错，但主要来自餐饮和地方政府教育，information 与 financial employment 反而继续下降。消费和就业的 headline 还没有崩，内部 breadth 却已经明显收窄。

过去几个季度，美国企业通过提价、控制招聘和压低成本，把通胀转化成了利润。但当消费者的储蓄缓冲耗尽，如果连续加息进一步打击需求，最先消失的就是企业提价能力。与此同时，利息、折旧和工资成本不会同步下降。

于是整个周期会开始反转：

需求降温，定价权消失；利润率见顶，EPS 开始下修；企业削减 capex，招聘转为裁员；收入下降再次压低消费，最终形成自我强化的衰退循环。

AI capex 是这条链条里最后、也是最重要的一根支柱。今年美国 capex 增量中超过一半来自 AI buildout。它同时支撑 GDP、企业利润、就业收入、信用扩张和股票估值。

这不是增长变得更加分散，而是整个经济越来越依赖同一台发动机。

更值得警惕的是，AI capex 正在从单纯依靠 hyperscaler 自由现金流，逐渐延伸到 neocloud、private credit、长期算力合同和项目融资。NVDA 也不再只是一个卖芯片的公司，它正在把产业周期与信用周期连接起来。

通过超过 $500bn 的第三方融资平台、约 $36bn 的 AI-cloud capacity commitments、take-or-pay、minimum-revenue guarantee 和 residual-value support，GPU 与长期算力合同正在被改造成可以评级、抵押和分发的金融资产。

这实际上是资产证券化的前置工程：先把未来的算力收入变成今天可以融资的抵押品，再用融资建设更多数据中心、购买更多 GPU，最后由新增产能继续支撑 NVDA 的收入与估值。

当算力供不应求、租金不断上涨时，这是一台不断自我强化的机器。但一旦 Warsh 开启连续加息，长端利率和信用成本上升，AI 收入增长无法覆盖融资与折旧成本，这台机器就会反向运转。

AI ROI 下滑，客户开始缩减需求；GPU 利用率、租金和二手残值下降；take-or-pay 合同被重谈；项目的 DSCR 和 LTV 被击穿；再融资渠道关闭；被迫出售的 GPU 又进一步压低抵押品价值。

同一个 demand shock 会同时打击三层资产：neocloud 的现金流、贷款人的抵押品，以及 NVDA 的订单与兜底义务。

NVDA 将一边面对新芯片销售减速，一边承担更多 capacity、lease 和 residual-value support；融资方开始提高 haircut，neocloud 被迫削减 capex，芯片订单进一步下降。牛市里的正反馈，就会变成信用收缩中的负反馈。

所以我谈论的“2008风险”，不是说 GPU 等于房子，而是两者拥有同一种 wrong-way risk：同一个经济冲击，同时打穿底层现金流、抵押品价值和信用创造能力。

2008 年真正摧毁金融体系的，也不是房价下跌本身，而是整个系统都把过去不断上涨的资产价格，当成了未来现金流和下一轮信贷扩张的基础。一旦底层资产停止升值，所有看起来分散出去的风险，最终都会沿着担保、杠杆和期限错配重新回到金融体系。

静态思维看到的是美国太强；周期思维看到的却是均值回归的起点正在靠近。

如果 Warsh 在这个位置重新开启加息周期，他打击的不只是当期需求，而是可能同时刺破利润周期与 AI 信用周期的顶部，把美国经济最后一台增长发动机，变成下一场衰退的金融加速器。

我认为这次CPI与FOMC 非常、非常危险。

假如 CPI 没有超级 cool，Fed 却继续按兵不动，而且拿不出清楚、可验证的 reaction function，那么市场先交易的不会是降息利好，而是 credibility risk。2Y 也许会先跌，但 10Y、30Y、term premium 和通胀补偿可能反向上行，长端替 Fed 完成紧缩。反过来，如果 Fed 加息 25bp，同时把点阵图明显上移、暗示后面还有几次，那么一次保险加息就会被市场重定价成 higher-for-longer，信用、投资和就业将在未来几个季度承受更大的滞后冲击。

我定义的 super-cool CPI 不是 headline 同比少一位小数，而是至少四件事一起发生：核心环比大致在 0.15%—0.20%或更低；shelter 与 core services ex-housing 不再加速；median、trimmed mean 和价格扩散度同步降温；关税、能源与电子设备的涨价没有向更广消费篮子传导。如果只有二手车、机票或某个波动分项贡献惊喜，我不会把它当作 Fed 可以放心 hold 的通行证。

低中收入群体已经开始被生活成本挤压，真正还在撑美国消费的，是中高收入群体。

问题恰恰也出在这里。

美国中高端消费现在很大一部分韧性，来自过去几年异常强的 equity wealth effect。股市涨，富裕家庭资产负债表变好，premium travel、restaurants、luxury、autos、leisure 这些消费自然还能撑住。

而过去两年美股最核心的边际驱动力，又恰恰是 AI。

所以美国现在其实存在一条非常重要的正反馈链：

AI capex → 科技股盈利预期 → 股市上涨 → 高收入财富效应 → 中高端消费。

这条链目前还没断。

但我觉得市场真正应该开始担心的，是它什么时候反转。

AI 现在的问题我已经讲过太多次，唯一的变现场景仍然只有coding，大量普通白领场景虽然有 usage，付费意愿和实际经济价值远没有 coding 那么清晰。

同时，开源模型越来越强、模型效率越来越高，最先被侵蚀的是闭源模型的 pricing power。

市场已经明显开始怀疑AI 最终产生的现金流，能不能 justify 今天这种级别的 capex。

如果未来 hyperscaler capex 增速开始明显下台阶，哪怕不是负增长，只是从 +50% 掉到 +15%，对美国 private investment 都会是很大的边际拖累。

更麻烦的是，一旦 AI capex 预期下修，科技股本身也会先杀估值。

于是原来的正反馈：

AI capex↑ → 股市↑ → 高收入消费↑

就可能反过来变成：

AI capex↓ → 科技股↓ → wealth effect↓ → 中高端消费↓。

而此时低中收入消费本来就已经在 real income squeeze 下减速。

我预计最迟2027年 H1，市场最终会痛苦地承认，Main Street consumption 已经在降速，同时 AI capex 和 equity wealth effect 也开始反转。

到那个时候，美国面对的就不再只是消费放缓，而是一个清晰的recession。

结合这两点，我认为接下来的一段时间，逢高做空会是一个更好的主意，直到ai产生新的killer app。
